**What the latest commit changed.** 311eab90ab did two things that matter here:

**Why it fails on Windows.** [claude_cli.py:219](tests/project_prompt/claude_cli.py:219) and [claude_cli.py:392](tests/project_prompt/claude_cli.py:392) create their temporary folders under `dir="/tmp"`. The runner listens on it, and [claude_mcp_stub.py](tests/project_prompt/claude_mcp_stub.py) connects to it. The stub is the fake MCP tool server the CLI launches, and it forwards each tool call back to the runner. macOS limits that path to about 104 characters, and its default temp folder is long, hence `/tmp`.

On Windows there are two separate problems: the folder path, and whether Python there supports `AF_UNIX` at all. My guess is that a localhost TCP socket on Windows only would be the safe fix, but I haven't checked that yet. The fix must leave the Mac behaviour as it is.

---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The claude-cli backend against a fake Messages endpoint: what the model
would receive, and the step rules through real MCP calls. Runs the installed
Claude Code CLI with a dummy API key aimed at a local server, so it needs no
login, sends nothing anywhere and costs nothing. Skipped when `claude` is not
on PATH. Run it after a CLI update: the resumed session is the CLI's own
internal format.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_claude_cli.py
"""

import http.server
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import threading
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)
cli = runner.claude_cli


class FakeMessages:
    """Answers each streamed request with the next scripted response (a list
    of content blocks) and keeps every request body."""

    def __init__(self, *responses):
        self.responses, self.bodies = list(responses), []
        fake = self

        class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *_):
                pass

            def do_HEAD(self):
                self.send_response(200)
                self.end_headers()

            def do_POST(self):
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0))))
                if not self.path.startswith("/v1/messages") or "count_tokens" in self.path or not body.get("stream"):
                    self.send_response(404)
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                fake.bodies.append(body)
                blocks = fake.responses.pop(0) if fake.responses else [{"type": "text", "text": "(nothing scripted)"}]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()

                def event(data):
                    self.wfile.write(f"event: {data['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode())

                event({"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": f"msg_{len(fake.bodies)}", "type": "message",
                       "role": "assistant", "model": body["model"], "content": [], "stop_reason": None,
                       "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}})
                for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
                    if block["type"] == "text":
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": block["text"]}})
                    else:
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block":
                               {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{len(fake.bodies)}_{index}", "name": block["name"],
                                "input": {}}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(block["input"])}})
                    event({"type": "content_block_stop", "index": index})
                stop = "tool_use" if any(block["type"] == "tool_use" for block in blocks) else "end_turn"
                event({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": stop, "stop_sequence": None},
                       "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}})
                event({"type": "message_stop"})

        self.server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()


def tool(name, arguments):
    return {"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.PREFIX + name, "input": arguments}


def plain(value):
    """A request's content without the CLI's cache markers."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [plain(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: plain(item) for key, item in value.items() if key != "cache_control"}
    return value


def conversation(body):
    """A request's messages without the CLI's own system turns (its
    environment note, and an empty one carrying the effort setting)."""
    return [message for message in plain(body["messages"]) if message["role"] != "system"]


def texts(body):
    for message in body["messages"]:
        content = message["content"]
        for block in [{"text": content}] if isinstance(content, str) else content:
            yield block.get("text") or json.dumps(block.get("content", ""))


class Split(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_recorded_point_splits(self):
        """Every point becomes a session and a last message, or a session
        ending on one deferred call; mid-turn points are the deferred ones."""
        for name, request in runner.REQUESTS.items():
            items = request["body"]["input"]
            history, last, deferred = cli.split(items)
            last_item = [item for item in items if item.get("role") != "developer"][-1]
            self.assertEqual(deferred is not None, last_item.get("type") == "function_call_output", name)
            self.assertEqual(last is None, deferred is not None, name)
            cli.messages(history + (last or []))  # every item has a Messages form


@unittest.skipIf(shutil.which("claude") is None, "the Claude Code CLI is not installed")
class ThroughTheCli(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_case(self, name, *responses):
        fake = FakeMessages(*responses)
        os.environ[cli.TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV] = fake.url
        try:
            verdict, detail, _log = runner.run_once_claude(name, "INSTRUCTIONS", "claude-opus-5-5", "medium")
        finally:
            del os.environ[cli.TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV]
            fake.close()
        return verdict, detail, fake.bodies

    def assertIsolated(self, body, tools):
        self.assertEqual(body["system"][-1]["text"], "INSTRUCTIONS")
        self.assertEqual([plain(t) for t in body["tools"]],
                         [{"name": cli.PREFIX + t["name"], "description": t["description"], "input_schema": t["parameters"]}
                          for t in tools])
        for text in texts(body):  # nothing of the developer's own Claude Code setup
            self.assertNotIn("CLAUDE.md", text)
            self.assertNotIn("Output Style", text)

    def test_a_point_mid_turn(self):
        """after-preview: the turn's calls and results are replayed as real
        turns, the last call's result comes through the stub, a read the model
        makes is answered from the recording, and its change ends the run."""
        request = runner.REQUESTS["after-preview"]
        preview = runner.last_result(request)["result"]
        verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
            "after-preview", [tool("workspace_inspect", {})],
            [tool("settings_apply_patch", {"expectedSessionId": preview["sessionId"],
                                           "expectedRevision": preview["revision"], "scope": "process",
                                           "changes": {change["key"]: change["after"] for change in preview["changes"]}})])
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        self.assertEqual(len(bodies), 2)
        self.assertIsolated(bodies[0], runner.TOOLS)
        history, _, deferred = cli.split(request["body"]["input"])
        expected = cli.messages(history)
        sent = conversation(bodies[0])
        self.assertEqual(sent[:len(expected)], expected)
        result = sent[len(expected)]["content"][0]
        self.assertEqual(result["tool_use_id"], deferred[0]["call_id"])
        self.assertEqual([block["text"] for block in result["content"]], deferred[1])
        answered = conversation(bodies[1])[-1]["content"][-1]
        recorded = next(answer["output"] for answer in request["answers"] if answer["tool"] == "workspace_inspect")
        self.assertEqual([block["text"] for block in answered["content"]], [recorded])

    def test_a_refused_call_gets_the_apps_refusal_through_the_stub(self):
        """advice-infill: a settings_search with a sessionId it does not take
        reaches the model as the app's refusal, through the stub, and the
        reply that follows is the step."""
        verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
            "advice-infill", [tool("settings_search", {"scope": "process", "query": "infill", "sessionId": "1"})],
            [{"type": "text", "text": "Use 15% infill."}])
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        refused = json.loads(conversation(bodies[1])[-1]["content"][-1]["content"][0]["text"])
        self.assertEqual(refused["error"]["code"], "invalid_arguments")
        self.assertIn("Not a parameter of this tool: sessionId.", refused["error"]["message"])

    def test_a_point_on_a_new_message(self):
        """model-opened-unnamed: the person's message goes in whole, the
        plate's picture as an image and the skill as a developer message, and
        the subscription judge reads the reply."""
        runner.CLAUDE_JUDGE = ("claude-opus-5-5", "medium")
        try:
            verdict, detail, bodies = self.run_case(
                "model-opened-unnamed", [{"type": "text", "text": "That looks like a rabbit. What is it for?"}],
                [{"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.STRUCTURED_OUTPUT, "input": {"answer": "yes", "why": "a rabbit"}}])
        finally:
            runner.CLAUDE_JUDGE = None
        self.assertEqual(verdict, runner.PASS, detail)
        self.assertIsolated(bodies[0], runner.TOOLS)
        _, last, _ = cli.split(runner.REQUESTS["model-opened-unnamed"]["body"]["input"])
        sent = conversation(bodies[0])
        self.assertEqual(sent, cli.messages(last))
        self.assertEqual([block["type"] for block in sent[0]["content"]], ["text", "text", "image", "text"])
        self.assertTrue(sent[0]["content"][-1]["text"].startswith("<developer_message>\n"))
        self.assertEqual(bodies[1]["system"][-1]["text"].split(",")[0], "You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person")

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).


The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree

  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.

  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,

The full run is now the subscription baseline, committed locally as adb6c6968a on top of 9d05d60eaf and not pushed. The commit changes only `baseline-claude-cli.json` and the prompt-test README.

- **`baseline-claude-cli.json`:** written by the runner from the saved results (`--compare … --record-baseline`). It has all 26 cases at 3 of 3, and unlike the old hand-made file it holds the SHA-256 of the prompt, tool list and recording. Future runs will be told when any of those three differs. I added a one-line `note`, as `baseline.json` has, saying the recording predates the `fitsSelectedBed` fix. Most of the file's large diff is formatting: the runner writes each case on several lines.
- **README:** the "Current subscription baseline" section now describes this run: the commit, the CLI version, about 5 minutes, and the token counts. It also records two findings: `print-this-no-purpose` going from 1 of 3 to 3 of 3, probably because of the Choices rule (untested), and the one bunny reply that mentioned the wrong "does not fit" report. The 2026-10-20 description moved to "Baseline history", as the README's re-recording rule asks.
- **Checks:** the runner's 44 offline tests pass, and comparing the saved run with the new file gives 0 worse and 0 better.

**Still open:** the original brief's Windows fix. `claude_cli.py` still puts its temporary folders under `/tmp` and uses a Unix socket, so the subscription backend still can't run on the Windows VM. It isn't needed for this comparison; it matters only if sessions on the VM should run the suite themselves.
